bullets.text: A landslide known as the Ashfell Slide occurred in the mining region of Dreth in the early hours of March 14, 2026.
A bench failure on the slope sent debris onto the lower road, damaging it and prompting warnings for the Withel terraces and Cranmoor.
No casualties were reported in the first four hours; about 60 households were evacuated from the Withel terraces and residents were moved out of Cranmoor.
Warnings and precautionary evacuations were in effect at the end of the window, with the cause of the slide and its attribution to mining activity not yet established.
A bench failure occurs at Ashfell and debris damages the lower road.
Authorities issue a warning for the Withel terraces and Cranmoor about two and a half hours later.
About 60 households are evacuated from the Withel terraces and residents are evacuated from Cranmoor.
Government sources confirm the lower road damage at the end of the window.
A bench failure on the Ashfell slope damaged the lower road below the slide.
About 60 households were evacuated from the Withel terraces, and residents were also evacuated from Cranmoor.
A landslide warning was issued for the Withel terraces and Cranmoor.
